input.rationale: New sourced discrepancy on the slow Accept path. handlePreAcceptReply acts on a reply carrying a higher ballot than the coordinator's: it increments lb.nacks and, once a majority nacks and the replica is the leader, calls makeBallot then bcastPrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:855-870). handleAcceptReply has the analogous block but it is unreachable: the preceding guard returns whenever lb.lastTriedBallot != areply.Ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026), so the following test areply.Ballot > lb.lastTriedBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1028-1035) can never be true. Consequently an Accept reply that reports a higher ballot (handleAccept replies with inst.bal, epaxos/epaxos.go:1001-1004) is silently dropped: no nack is counted, the coordinator's ballot is not raised, and no Prepare is issued. A coordinator stuck at its Accept ballot then cannot assemble acceptOKs+1 > N/2 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1040) and the instance can only progress through the executeCommands recovery timer. I am raising this as a Candidate rather than a claimed defect because the stall may be bounded by that timer and the legality of a concurrent higher-ballot AcceptReply is not yet sourced.

The remaining question is whether this can stall an instance long enough to matter, given the executeCommands recovery timer.

No TryPreAccept exchange can occur, so no defer cycle can arise through the mechanism the guard was written to protect and no recovery stall follows from the inert guard. The original observation stands (possibleQuorum is never set true and the loop indexes a constant), but it has no observable consequence here, so the Candidate is explained with no defect. question_candidates.stop_reason: Source investigation answers the reachability premise negatively for the fault model this code implements, so the Candidate is explained rather than escalated. handleCommit's NOOP-repropose branch dereferences inst.lb.clientProposals with no nil check (epaxos/epaxos.go:1092), and newInstanceDefault leaves lb nil, so the dereference would panic if it were reached with a placeholder. But the branch is guarded by commit.Replica == r.Id, i.e. the receiver is the row owner of the instance, and the row owner is the only creator of entries in its own row: handlePropose allocates into r.crtInstance[r.Id] (epaxos/epaxos.go:724-749) and startPhase1 installs InstanceSpace[replica][instance] together with a fresh LeaderBookkeeping (lb) before bcastPreAccept (epaxos/epaxos.go:751-779). Every other path that can produce a Commit for row R with a NOOP command goes through a recovery leader's startPhase1(preply.Replica, ...) (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1312), which only ever recovers an instance (R,i) that already existed, and an instance (R,i) can only originate from R's own proposal because handlePropose always uses r.Id. crtInstance[R] is likewise only advanced together with creating the entry. So in a crash-free execution the receiver's own-row entry always has non-nil lb, and the nil-lb placeholder state on one's own row requires the row owner to have lost its own instance, which is the durability/restart path (Durable false, replay unread) rather than a legal history of the modelled faults. The missing guard is a real latent robustness gap and I keep it visible as a remaining item, but I do not claim a reachable defect.

selections.rationale: First pass on the EPaxos replica. Traced both core lines (A1 qualified support for decision formation; A2 per-instance ballot/authority transitions) plus the A3 recovery, A5 execution, A6 persistence and A7 client paths that connect them, and wrote a usable partial map in map.json. Formation: handlePropose allocates an own-row instance, startPhase1 pre-accepts with conflict-derived (seq,deps), and handlePreAcceptReply fast-commits on an agreeing fast quorum on the initial ballot (COMMITTED) or falls back to Accept needing a majority. Context/authority: authority is per instance via bal/vbal; acceptors reject lower ballots, makeBallot raises the ballot, and recovery issues Prepare then either accept-commits, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase1 from the highest-VBallot replies. Connection: recovery rebuilds the same F-PREACCEPT-STATE facts the formation path consumes, CommittedUpTo exposes a stable committed prefix, and execution consumes only the committed dependency graph, so old client proposals are carried through lb.clientProposals and re-proposed on a NOOP commit. Several local anomalies were recorded as sourced unknowns rather than defects: the handlePreAccept Status>=ACCEPTED & Cmds==nil branch writes InstanceSpace[LeaderId] instead of the instance being handled; the subcase-3 and subcase-4 guards in handlePrepareReply are textually identical; and the notInQuorum loop in handleTryPreAcceptReply indexes possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] instead of possibleQuorum[q]. None is yet grounded as an applicable violated responsibility.

feedback.answered: Core relationships recorded. A1: qualified support for decision formation is a coordinator-local sequence of startPhase1 (PREACCEPTED with conflict-derived seq/deps) plus PreAcceptReply aggregation; the decision is COMMITTED only when a fast quorum agrees, the trial ballot is the initial ballot, and (N>7) committed deps are present, otherwise the Accept phase resolves by majority. A2: authority is a per-instance ballot; acceptors only accept ballot >= stored bal, a coordinator that observes a higher ballot raises its own via makeBallot and issues Prepare, and recovery reconstructs (vbal,status,seq,deps) from a slow quorum before re-entering accept or phase1. Connection: recovery reproduces the same per-instance pre-accept facts the formation path consumes, the committed prefix (CommittedUpTo) and idempotent handleCommit bound re-decisions, and execution consumes only the committed dependency graph, with old client proposals carried in lb.clientProposals.
remaining: Whether the handlePreAccept branch that writes InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][preAccept.Instance].Cmds can ever run with LeaderId != Replica, and if so whether it mutates a wrong or nil slot (safety-relevant).
Whether the identical class-3/class-4 conditions in handlePrepareReply make the TryPreAccept recovery sub-case unreachable, and if so what a concurrent-conflict recovery would do instead.
Whether the notInQuorum loop in handleTryPreAcceptReply (always testing possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId]) can let a real deferred recovery cycle through.
Membership (A4) and thrifty/quorum-file selection: which quorum thresholds are active at runtime, since the fast/slow commit predicates depend on FastQuorumSize/SlowQuorumSize.
Durability (A6): the restart replay path and the apparent bal/vbal byte-offset overlap in recordInstanceMetadata are unread.

formation.explanation: A coordinator pre-accepts a batch in its own row (B-PROPOSE/B-PHASE1), then aggregates PreAcceptReply: if the fast quorum agrees on seq/deps (allEqual), the trial ballot is the initial ballot, and (for N>7) all committed deps are present, it fast-commits; otherwise it enters Accept and needs a majority. Both paths produce a concrete per-instance (Cmds, Seq, Deps) recorded as F-DECISION/F-COMMITTED and propagated by Commit.

context.explanation: Authority is per instance, carried by bal/vbal (F-BALLOT). A coordinator acquires the trial ballot in startPhase1; acceptors only accept a ballot >= their stored bal, so a higher-ballot message transfers authority away from a stalled coordinator. Recovery (A3) raises the ballot via makeBallot, issues Prepare, and reconstructs the instance's (vbal, status, seq, deps) from a slow quorum, then re-uses the formation paths. Established COMMITTED instances are not re-decided (handleCommit returns early), and CommittedUpTo exposes a stable committed prefix to acceptors and coordinators.

connection.explanation: Recovery and formation share the same per-instance facts: a recovering coordinator rebuilds F-PREACCEPT-STATE from the highest-VBallot Prepare replies and then either takes the slow Accept path, TryPreAccept (guarded by findPreAcceptConflicts), or restarts phase1 with a NOOP/old command. Committed support is the boundary: acceptors report CommittedUpTo, handleCommit is idempotent for already-COMMITTED instances, and execution (B-EXEC) consumes only the committed dependency graph. Thus old requests survive via lb.clientProposals carried into recovery and re-proposed on a NOOP commit, and established decisions constrain all later formation by fixing (Cmds, Seq, Deps) and the contiguous committed prefix.

selections.rationale: Source investigation answers the reachability premise negatively for the fault model this code implements, so the Candidate is explained rather than escalated. handleCommit's NOOP-repropose branch dereferences inst.lb.clientProposals with no nil check (epaxos/epaxos.go:1092), and newInstanceDefault leaves lb nil, so the dereference would panic if it were reached with a placeholder. But the branch is guarded by commit.Replica == r.Id, i.e. the receiver is the row owner of the instance, and the row owner is the only creator of entries in its own row: handlePropose allocates into r.crtInstance[r.Id] (epaxos/epaxos.go:724-749) and startPhase1 installs InstanceSpace[replica][instance] together with a fresh LeaderBookkeeping (lb) before bcastPreAccept (epaxos/epaxos.go:751-779). Every other path that can produce a Commit for row R with a NOOP command goes through a recovery leader's startPhase1(preply.Replica, ...) (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1312), which only ever recovers an instance (R,i) that already existed, and an instance (R,i) can only originate from R's own proposal because handlePropose always uses r.Id. crtInstance[R] is likewise only advanced together with creating the entry. So in a crash-free execution the receiver's own-row entry always has non-nil lb, and the nil-lb placeholder state on one's own row requires the row owner to have lost its own instance, which is the durability/restart path (Durable false, replay unread) rather than a legal history of the modelled faults. The missing guard is a real latent robustness gap and I keep it visible as a remaining item, but I do not claim a reachable defect.

feedback.answered: The handleCommit nil-lb dereference is not reachable in the modelled fault model. The branch requires commit.Replica == r.Id, and the row owner is the sole creator of its own row's entries (handlePropose uses r.Id; startPhase1 installs the entry and its lb before broadcasting), while recovery (startPhase1 from handlePrepareReply sub-cases 5/6) only recovers instances that already existed. A NOOP Commit for one's own row therefore implies a row-owner entry with non-nil lb, so inst.lb.clientProposals cannot be dereferenced on a placeholder without the row owner having lost state (restart/durability).

context.explanation: Authority is per instance, carried by bal/vbal (F-BALLOT). A coordinator acquires the trial ballot in startPhase1; acceptors only accept a ballot >= their stored bal, so a higher-ballot message transfers authority away from a stalled coordinator. Recovery (A3) raises the ballot via makeBallot, issues Prepare, and reconstructs the instance's (vbal, status, seq, deps) from a slow quorum, then re-uses the formation paths. Established COMMITTED instances are not re-decided (handleCommit returns early), and CommittedUpTo exposes a stable committed prefix to acceptors and coordinators.

connection.explanation: Recovery and formation share the same per-instance facts: a recovering coordinator rebuilds F-PREACCEPT-STATE from the highest-VBallot Prepare replies and then either takes the slow Accept path, TryPreAccept (guarded by findPreAcceptConflicts), or restarts phase1 with a NOOP/old command. Committed support is the boundary: acceptors report CommittedUpTo, handleCommit is idempotent for already-COMMITTED instances, and execution (B-EXEC) consumes only the committed dependency graph. Thus old requests survive via lb.clientProposals carried into recovery and re-proposed on a NOOP commit, and established decisions constrain all later formation by fixing (Cmds, Seq, Deps) and the contiguous committed prefix.

A NOOP Commit for one's own row therefore implies a row-owner entry with non-nil lb, so inst.lb.clientProposals cannot be dereferenced on a placeholder without the row owner having lost state (restart/durability).

selections.rationale: New sourced discrepancy on the slow Accept path. handlePreAcceptReply acts on a reply carrying a higher ballot than the coordinator's: it increments lb.nacks and, once a majority nacks and the replica is the leader, calls makeBallot then bcastPrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:855-870). handleAcceptReply has the analogous block but it is unreachable: the preceding guard returns whenever lb.lastTriedBallot != areply.Ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026), so the following test areply.Ballot > lb.lastTriedBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1028-1035) can never be true. Consequently an Accept reply that reports a higher ballot (handleAccept replies with inst.bal, epaxos/epaxos.go:1001-1004) is silently dropped: no nack is counted, the coordinator's ballot is not raised, and no Prepare is issued. A coordinator stuck at its Accept ballot then cannot assemble acceptOKs+1 > N/2 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1040) and the instance can only progress through the executeCommands recovery timer. I am raising this as a Candidate rather than a claimed defect because the stall may be bounded by that timer and the legality of a concurrent higher-ballot AcceptReply is not yet sourced.

feedback.answered: The higher-ballot handling on the Accept reply path is dead: handleAcceptReply returns on any ballot mismatch before its greater-than test, so a reply reporting a higher ballot is dropped without a nack, a ballot raise, or a Prepare, unlike the equivalent PreAccept reply path which does escalate. The remaining question is whether this can stall an instance long enough to matter, given the executeCommands recovery timer.
remaining: Whether a higher-ballot AcceptReply can legally arrive while the coordinator is in ACCEPTED status at its own ballot (concurrent recovery of the same instance).
